merges.reason: 2026-10-22 audit followup merge 1/2: one incident. Both stories describe the ConnectWise Cloud Backup / SkyKick API-secret compromise where a stolen vendor credential signed in to Microsoft 365 tenants as the application with no user MFA (loser events: securityonline.info 'Hackers abused a SkyKick API secret in a ConnectWise Cloud Backup breach, accessing 300+ Microsoft 365 tenants and planting rogue app credentials' + diesec.com 'a compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential signed in to Microsoft 365 as the app, no user MFA, 162+ tenants'). The canonical carries the same incident across 35 events / 20 sources since 2026-10-16 (Sophos X-Ops token sweep, BleepingComputer 'Hackers breach Microsoft 365 tenants via ConnectWise supply-chain attack') and is digest-linked 10-17, 10-18, 10-20; the loser has 2 events / 2 sources, no digest link. Same vendor, same credential, same M365 app sign-in, same tenant counts.

2026-10-22 audit followup merge 2/2: one incident. Unauthorized access to TeamUpdraft's website over the weekend of 2026-10-17/18 exposed the customer database holding UpdraftCentral connection keys (also UpdraftVault/UpdraftClone), which were then used to send trusted remote-management commands and install malicious plugins on connected WordPress sites. The canonical is the vendor's own disclosure (teamupdraft.com security-incident-october-2026, first_seen 2026-10-19T16:07Z, 4 sources, digest-linked 10-20); the loser is downstream coverage of the same key theft (bleepingcomputer.com 'Stolen UpdraftCentral keys used to backdoor WordPress sites', gbhackers.com, Wordfence/Nethemba reports), 7 events / 2 sources, no digest link. Same victim vendor, same key class, same 10-17/18 intrusion window.
